Women were allowed jobs, but mostly those without family support chose to pursue them, because they couldn't land a husband who went through the long grind of becoming a master at his art. There are records of female artisans. But between choosing 10-15 years of what was essentially slave labour from an early age on and becoming a housewife of someone who already did all that, most chose the latter. Some probably didnt chose, but a lot did.

Opression was a hurdle, sure, but there are women who took risks and overcame it. Famous figures for example. Women were allowed trades in the middle ages, but it was a long and hard way to get to where they could have their own business. It was mostly orphaned women who took up trades because they didn't have a choice a lot of times. There are even historical records of female artisans. But as I explained to another user, those who had a family chose in many cases the comfort of marrying a man who had already went through all the trouble of learning a trade. They could have always ran away if they really didn't want to marry someone, which would be taking a risk. You'd lose your home, your family, anything you couldn't take with you, all your friends might hate you, but it wasn't impossible to overcome. Was it hard? Absolutely, but it's not like they put you in chains and drag you to the altar.
